title: Electron Microscopy of 2D Layered Double Hydroxides for Antigen Loading and Release
content: Clays are abundant, low cost and environment friendly. They have been used as remedies for several diseases for a rather long time e.g., ulcer treatments, antidiarrheal cure and blood purification [1]. They are an emerging class of biomaterials owing to their thickness that enables nanoscale characteristics, charged and biocompatible surfaces, and well-defined compositions [1]. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are anionic nanosized heterostructures (2D hydrotalcite clays) with special application in medicine. They normally have layers with inter-lamellar spacings that can be used for drug delivery, immunotherapy and cancer treatment. Yet, the knowledge about their potential is still poor. A complete investigation has been performed with a set of different LDHs but in the present investigation, only the results related to transmission electron microscopy will be discussed. They have been synthesized by using co-precipitation and hydrothermal treatment. Nanoclays can be either cationic or anionic types according to their layer charge [2]. Cationic clays mostly consist of silicate clays (laponites, kaolinite, and montmorillonite (MMT) [3]. Cationic clays are made of aminosilicate layers with a negative charge and show a cationic exchange property and surface acidity [4]. Anionic clays are made of positively charged layers that can intercalate anions. Anionic clays can be applied to load anionic biomolecules. The anionic category of 2D nanoclay includes layered double hydroxides (LDHs). The positively charged anionic clays, i.e. LDH facilitate better interactions with negatively charged bacterial membrane leading to anti-bacterial activity. The LDHs have been loaded with ovalbumin (OVA) and their performance is being compared to a commercial adjuvant, alum. Zn-Al and Mg-Al LDHs have shown over 80% antigen encapsulation efficiency, with Zn-Al LDHs showing around a 15% enhancement in OV-loading compared to alum. Zn-Al LDHs-OVA and Mg-Al LDHs-OVA samples have been more avidly and rapidly taken up into MCF-7 breast cancer cells and primary spleen cells than pure OVA or OVA loaded alum. These materials have shown a slow and more controlled release of antigen with time. Such an investigation study has demonstrated the potential of LDH to serve as adjuvants for vaccination and cancer immunotherapy.
